summary: Bulgaria is a unitary state with a flat 10% personal income tax, a flat 10% corporate income tax and a 20% VAT. The State collects almost everything, and the social contributions, paid by employers and employees, are the second-largest flow after VAT. Municipalities levy the real estate tax, the vehicle tax and a tax on donations and property acquisitions.
structureNote: The figures are the Commission’s National Tax List for 2024, in leva. The sale of emission trading permits (BGN 2,293 million) is left out. The social contributions are drawn under the State. The list’s Eurostat counterpart for Bulgaria in July 2026 is in euro; converted at BGN 1.95583 per euro its totals match the list. Bulgaria is not an OECD member, so this folio has no harmonised OECD layer.

theme.motifNote: Topographic contour lines over the outline of Bulgaria (the generic motif; no bespoke art yet).

levels.description: The National Assembly legislates all taxes; the National Revenue Agency (NRA) and the Customs Agency collect them, and the NRA collects the social contributions for the National Social Security Institute and the National Health Insurance Fund.
levels.fiscalPower: Taxes are set by law; municipalities set rates only within the ranges of the Local Taxes and Fees Act.

levels.description: The only tier of local self-government. They levy the real estate tax, the vehicle tax, the tax on donations and on acquisitions of property for consideration, and small taxes.
levels.fiscalPower: Municipal councils set the tax rates within the ranges fixed by the Local Taxes and Fees Act.
